rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary points to Jesus because he is the one who will answer when they address him.
rows.anchor: أي هو الذي يجيبكم إذا ناطقتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view identifies Zakariya as the person who challenged Jesus to speak.
rows.anchor: كان المستنطق لعيسى زكريا عليه السلام

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the people grew angry at Mary's gesture and thought her mockery worse than her alleged adultery.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي : لما أشارت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the nursing infant stopped suckling, faced the people, leaned on his left, and pointed with his forefinger.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان يرضع ، فلما سمع ذلك ترك الرضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Jesus spoke then remained silent until he reached the age when children ordinarily speak.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كلمهم بذلك ، ثم لم يتكلم حتى بلغ مبلغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here kāna places the statement in an unspecified past time, narrowed to the near past by the discourse's expression of wonder.
rows.anchor: كان } لإيقاع مضمون الجملة في زمان ماض مبهم يصلح لقريبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nukallimu recounts a past convention: they ask when anyone had ever spoken to an infant in a cradle.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر : أن يكون { نكلم } حكاية حال ماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first makes Jesus declare himself God's servant, refuting the Christians; al-kitāb means the Gospel.
rows.anchor: أنطقه الله أولا بأنه عبد الله ردا لقول النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Jesus received prophethood in infancy: God perfected his intellect and commissioned him as a child, as the verse's surface suggests.
rows.anchor: فقيل : أعطيها في طفوليته : أكمل الله عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the past wording to mean prophethood was already decreed, or that an inevitable future is spoken of as accomplished.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه إن ذلك سبق في قضائه . أو جعل الآتي

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report explains blessedness as being beneficial wherever one is.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 661 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss of blessed is a teacher of good.
rows.anchor: معلما للخير . وقرىء ( وبرا ) عن أبي نهيك

rows.speaker: أبو نهيك
rows.claim: Abu Nuhayk reads wa-barran and understands Jesus himself to be righteousness because of his abundant goodness.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( وبرا ) عن أبي نهيك ، جعل ذاته برا لفرط بره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative barran can be governed by a verb equivalent in meaning to awṣānī, since charging him with prayer and making him righteous are treated alike.
rows.anchor: وهو كلفني ؛ لأن أوصاني بالصلاة وكلفنيها واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-salām may refer back to the peace just mentioned: the peace addressed to Yahya in three moments is addressed to Jesus too.
rows.anchor: أدخل لام التعريف لتعرفه بالذكر قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading uses the generic article to insinuate a curse on Mary's accusers: peace is uniquely on Jesus, implying its opposite for them.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن يكون هذا التعريف تعريضا باللعنة على متهمي مريم

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read qawl al-haqq in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر { قول الحق } بالنصب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading is qāla al-haqq, followed by wa-qāla Allāh.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود ( قال الحق ) وقال الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads qawl al-haqq with a nominative qāf, as in al-Anʿām 6:73.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : ( قول الحق ) ، بضم القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms qawl, qāl, and qawl are synonymous, like the variant forms of rahb.
rows.anchor: والقول والقال والقول بمعنى واحد ، كالرهب والرهب والرهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative may be a second predicate, an apposition, or the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: وارتفاعه على أنه خبر بعد خبر ، أو بدل ، أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is praise if Jesus is meant by God's Word, or an emphatic verbal noun affirming truth if the phrase means true and truthful speech.
rows.anchor: وأما انتصابه فعلى المدح إن فسر بكلمة الله ، وعلى أنه مصدر مؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is called God's Word because he was born through God's word kun without a human father; the cause is named for its effect, as grass is called sky and fat dew.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يولد إلا بكلمة الله وحدها ، وهي قوله ( كن ) من غير واسطة أب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If qawl al-haqq refers to Jesus, al-Haqq may be God's name or mean firmness and truth; the following clause supports truth as the sense.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل إذا أريد بقول الحق عيسى ، أن يكون الحق اسم الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamترون means they doubt; al-mirya means doubt.
rows.anchor: يشكون . والمرية : الشك . أو يتمارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the form yatomārūn means that they dispute with one another.
rows.anchor: أو يتمارون : يتلاحقون ، قالت اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants are described as Jews calling Jesus a lying sorcerer and Christians calling him God's son and one of three.
rows.anchor: قالت اليهود : ساحر كذاب ، وقالت النصارى : ابن الله وثالث ثلاثة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reads tamtarūn as a direct address, 'you dispute'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : ( تمترون )

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading adds that people had disputed about Jesus.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب : ( قول الحق الذي كان الناس فيه يتمرون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes Christians by showing that offspring from God is impossible and inconceivable to reason.
rows.anchor: كذب النصارى وبكتهم بالدلالة على انتفاء الولد عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A being who creates anything by kun is unlike an animal that begets offspring.
rows.anchor: بأن من إذا أراد شيئا من الأجناس كلها أوجده بكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's saying kun is metaphorical: His will is followed inevitably by existence, like an obeyed ruler's order being carried out.
rows.anchor: والقول ههنا مجاز ، ومعناه : أن إرادته للشيء يتبعها كونه لا محالة

rows.speaker: المدنيون وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read inna with fatḥ, meaning 'because He is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him,' comparable to 72:18.
rows.anchor: قرأ المدنيون وأبو عمرو بفتح إن ومعناه : ولأنه ربي وربكم فاعبدوه

rows.speaker: الاستار وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They read inna with kasr as an independent sentence.
rows.anchor: والاستار وأبو عبيدة بالكسر على الابتداء

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading has inna Allāha with kasr and no conjunction.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبي ( إن الله ) ، بالكسر بغير واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant bi-anna Allāha means 'because of that,' giving the reason to worship God.
rows.anchor: و ( بأن الله ) ، أي : بسبب ذلك فاعبدوه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the factions as Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: الاحزاب } اليهود والنصارى عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the factions as the three Christian groups: Nestorians, Jacobites, and Melkites.
rows.anchor: وقيل النصارى لتحزبهم ثلاث فرق : نسطورية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says groups who had united against prophets differed over Jesus when his story was recounted.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : الذين تحزبوا على الأنبياء لما قص عليهم قصة عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great day's scene may mean their witnessing the terror of the resurrection's reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: من شهودهم هول الحساب والجزاء في يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mashhad may mean the place or the time of witnessing, or the resurrection gathering place.
rows.anchor: أو من مكان الشهود فيه وهو الموقف . أو من وقت الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean the Day's testimony against them by angels, prophets, and their own tongues and limbs for disbelief and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: وأن تشهد عليهم الملائكة والأنبياء وألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as the place or time of testimony, or as what they said and testified about Jesus and his mother.
rows.anchor: أو من مكان الشهادة أو وقتها . وقيل : هو ما قالوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not described as marveling; rather, the people's hearing and sight on that day will be astonishing after their worldly deafness and blindness.
rows.anchor: لا يوصف الله تعالى بالتعجب وإنما المراد أن أسماعهم وأبصارهم يومئذ جدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the expression threatens them with what they will hear and see that will distress them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه التهديد بما سيسمعون ويبصرون مما يسوءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit word al-ẓālimūn replaces a pronoun to show that neglecting useful hearing and sight is an especially grave injustice.
rows.anchor: أوقع الظاهر أعني الظالمين موقع الضمير : إشعارا بأن لا ظلم أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clear error here means neglecting to look and listen.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالضلال المبين : إغفال النظر والاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter is finished when the reckoning ends and the two groups depart for Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: فرغ من الحساب وتصادر الفريقان إلى الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked when the matter is decided, the Prophet answers: when the ram is slaughtered as both groups watch.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل عنه أي عن قضاء الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh may be appositional to yawm or governed in the accusative by al-ḥasra.
rows.anchor: وإذ بدل من يوم الحسرة . أو منصوب بالحسرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan connects 'while they are heedless' to their being in clear error; the warning is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: متعلق بقوله في ضلال مبين عن الحسن . وأنذرهم : اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the warning concerns their heedless, unbelieving state and may refer to their death and ruined homes or the destruction of their bodies and earth.
rows.anchor: أنذرهم على هذه الحال غافلين غير مؤمنين يحتمل أنه يميتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq is an intensive form, like ḍaḥīk and naṭīq; it signals Abraham's abundant truthfulness and belief in God's unseen matters, signs, books, and messengers.
rows.anchor: الصديق : من أبنية المبالغة . ونظيره الضحيك والنطيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says Abraham's belief chiefly favored the books and messengers: he affirmed all prophets and scriptures and was himself a prophet, as in 37:37.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجحان والغلبة في هذا التصديق للكتب والرسل أي : كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he was eloquent in truthfulness, the central quality of prophethood, and one who affirmed God's signs and miracles.
rows.anchor: أو كان بليغا في الصدق ، لأن ملاك أمر النبوة الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description is a parenthetical clause between the antecedent and its apposition, Abraham.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة وقعت اعتراضا بين المبدل منه وبدله ، أعني إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'when he said' can attach to kāna or to ṣiddīqan nabiyyan.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق إذ بكان أو بصديقا نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Messenger in the Book means reciting Abraham's account to people, as in 26:69; God already mentions him by revealing it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بذكر الرسول إياه وقصته في الكتاب أن يتلو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in yā-abati substitutes for the possessive yāʾ; ya-abatī is avoided to prevent combining the substitute with what it replaces.
rows.anchor: عوض من ياء الإضافة ، ولا يقال : يا أبتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A form yā-abatā is also proposed, with alif replacing yāʾ; Sibawayh compares the compensatory pattern to aynuq.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يا أبتا ، لكون الألف بدلا من الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham arranges his counsel with exceptional coherence, gentleness, tact, courtesy, and good manners, following God's own counsel.
rows.anchor: كيف رتب الكلام معه في أحسن اتساق ، وساقه أرشق مساق

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God told Abraham, His close friend, to perfect his manners even toward unbelievers, promising him shelter beneath the Throne and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham first asks why his father worships, to awaken him to the grave persistence and excess of his error.
rows.anchor: طلب منبه على تماديه ، موقظ لإفراطه وتناهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a living, discerning, hearing, seeing, powerful created being is not fit for worship or lordship, even if an angel or prophet.
rows.anchor: لاستخف عقل من أهله للعبادة ووصفه بالربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is the highest veneration and belongs only to the ultimate benefactor, creator, provider, life-giver, death-giver, rewarder, and punisher.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن العبادة هي غاية التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship directed elsewhere is injustice, defiance, error, disbelief, and departure from clear truth.
rows.anchor: لم يكن إلا ظلما وعتوا وغيا وكفرا وجحودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inert idol plainly cannot hear praise, see worship, avert harm, or meet a need.
rows.anchor: فلا يسمع يا عابده ذكرك له وثناءك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham next invites his father gently to truth without calling him ignorant or himself exceptionally learned; he says he has some guidance his father lacks and can lead him safely.
rows.anchor: فلم يسم أباه بالجهل المفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He then warns that Satan, disobedient to the Beneficent who gave his father every blessing, misled him into idolatry; in effect, the father worships Satan.
rows.anchor: ورطك في هذه الضلالة وأمرك بها وزينها لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of his intense devotion to God, Abraham mentions Satan's offense against God rather than Satan's enmity toward Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر من جنايتي الشيطان إلا التي تختص منهما برب العزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finally, Abraham warns of the consequence without bluntly declaring punishment certain, using the courteous formulation 'I fear that a punishment may touch you'.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يصرح بأن العقاب لاحق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God's pleasure greater than reward supports treating allegiance to Satan, the opposite of that pleasure, as worse than punishment itself.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن رضوان الله أكبر من الثواب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of Abraham's four counsels begins yā-abati as a plea for closeness and compassion.
rows.anchor: صدر كل نصيحة من النصائح الأربع بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mā lā yasmaʿ and mā lam ya'tika, mā may be relative or descriptive; the object of 'hears' and 'sees' is omitted and not intended.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون موصولة وموصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayʾan can be an accusative verbal noun meaning any benefit, with a parallel sense supplied for the preceding verbs.
rows.anchor: أن يكون في موضع المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, shayʾan is a direct object, following the expression aghna ʿannī wajhak.
rows.anchor: أن يكون مفعولا به من قولهم : أغن عني وجهك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that knowledge 'came' to Abraham implies that his knowledge was newly acquired.
rows.anchor: ما لم يأتك } فيه تجدد العلم عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham's proofs and tactful counsel, his father answers with harsh disbelief, calls him by name, and does not reciprocate yā-abati with a tender 'my son'.
rows.anchor: أقبل عليه الشيخ بفظاظة الكفر وغلظة العناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In arāghib anta, the predicate precedes the subject because the question of abandoning the idols is foremost to the father; the order conveys surprise and rejection.
rows.anchor: وقدم الخبر على المبتدأ في قوله : { أراغب أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exchange comforts the Prophet regarding similar treatment from his own people.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا سلوان وثلج لصدر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La-arjumannaka may mean I will insult you with my tongue, as a rajīm is one cast out by cursing.
rows.anchor: لأرمينك بلساني ، يريد الشتم والذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it threatens to kill him by stoning or drive him away by throwing stones; rajm fundamentally means throwing stones.
rows.anchor: أو لأقتلنك ، من رجم الزاني . أو لأطردنك رميا بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maliyyan can mean for a long time, from malāh, or a long-lasting departure before the father beats him so he cannot leave; the phrase can mean able to endure something.
rows.anchor: زمانا طويلا من الملاوة : أو مليا بالذهاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-hjurnī coordinates with an omitted 'beware of me,' implied by the threat la-arjumannaka.
rows.anchor: لأن { لارجمنك } تهديد وتقريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salāmun ʿalayka may be a farewell and separation, as in 28:55 and 25:63, showing that one may leave someone being advised in such circumstances.
rows.anchor: سلام توديع ومتاركة ، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham prays for his father's safety to win him over, as shown by his promise to seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: دعا له بالسلامة استمالة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the promise of forgiveness presupposed repentance from disbelief, as religious commands addressed to unbelievers presuppose faith and prerequisites such as ablution or the zakat threshold.
rows.anchor: قالوا أراد اشتراط التوبة عن الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Abraham sought forgiveness because his father promised to believe, citing 26:86 and the account of a promise in 9:114.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : إنما استغفر له بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that only revelation forbids seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever; reason permits the promise and fulfillment before that prohibition, as 60:4 indicates.
rows.anchor: إن الذي منع من الاستغفار للكافر إنما هو السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abraham had conditioned his promise on faith, it would not have been condemned as an exception to the required example.
rows.anchor: فلو كان شارطا للإيمان لم يكن مستنكرا

rows.speaker: حماد الراوية
rows.claim: Hamād's reading, waʿadahā abāhu, supports taking Abraham as the one who promised his father.
rows.anchor: قراءة حماد الراوية : وعدها أباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafiyyan means exceptionally kind and gracious; the verb is used for being kind to someone.
rows.anchor: البليغ في البر والإلطاف ، حفي به وتحفى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's separation means migration to Syria; duʿāʾ here means worship, since prayer is part and one of worship's means, as 19:49 confirms.
rows.anchor: أراد بالاعتزال المهاجرة إلى الشام

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that supplication is worship.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 664 ) ( الدعاء هو العبادة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, duʿāʾ means the supplication recorded in 26:83–89; Abraham hints that his family is wretched in invoking idols, while his own hope is expressed humbly with ʿasā.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الدعاء الذي حكاه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever leaves unbelieving, wicked people for God's sake loses nothing: God compensates him with believing prophetic children.
rows.anchor: ما خسر على الله أحد ترك الكفار الفسقة لوجهه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses God's mercy here as prophethood.
rows.anchor: من رحمتنا } هي النبوة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the mercy as wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي : المال والولد ، وتكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the mercy broadly includes every religious and worldly good they received.
rows.anchor: وتكون عامة في كل خير ديني ودنيوي أوتوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān ṣidq means good praise; 'tongue' stands for what the tongue produces, just as 'hand' can stand for a gift.
rows.anchor: لسان الصدق : الثناء الحسن . وعبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line uses lisān to mean a message or letter.
rows.anchor: إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Abraham's prayer for a good name in later generations, making him a model claimed by all religions, as 22:78, 2:135, and 16:123 show.
rows.anchor: استجاب الله دعوته { واجعل لي لسان صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Abraham's descendants the same distinction, raising their remembrance and praise as He raised his.
rows.anchor: وأعطى ذلك ذريته فأعلى ذكرهم وأثنى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasr, mukhliṣ means one who purifies worship from idolatry and show, or one who devotes himself wholly to God.
rows.anchor: المخلص بالكسر : الذي أخلص العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥ, mukhlaṣ means one whom God has purified.
rows.anchor: وبالفتح : الذي أخلصه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger is a prophet given a scripture; a prophet conveys God's message without necessarily having a scripture, as Joshua illustrates.
rows.anchor: الرسول : الذي معه كتاب من الأنبياء : والنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ayman can mean the right-hand side, or derive from Yemen/blessing as an adjective for the Mount or its side.
rows.anchor: الأيمن من اليمين : أي من ناحيته اليمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing Moses near for private conversation resembles a dignitary drawing someone close; God spoke to him without an angelic intermediary.
rows.anchor: حيث كلمه بغير واسطة ملك

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says Moses was brought so near that he heard the pen writing the Torah scrape.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي العالية قربه حتى سمع صريف القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min raḥmatinā can mean 'because of Our mercy and compassion for Moses,' or 'some of Our mercy,' as in 19:50.
rows.anchor: من أجل رحمتنا له وترأفنا عليه : وهبنا له هرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second reading, akhāhu is an apposition and Hārūn clarifies it, as in 'I saw a man, your brother Zayd'.
rows.anchor: على هذا الوجه بدل . و { هارون } عطف بيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Aaron was older than Moses, so the gift was Aaron's support and assistance.
rows.anchor: كذا عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail is singled out for promise-keeping as an honor despite the trait being shared by other prophets, and because it was especially famous in him.
rows.anchor: ذكر إسماعيل عليه السلام بصدق الوعد وإن كان ذلك موجودا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Ismail promised a companion to wait in one place and kept waiting for a year.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : أنه وعد صاحبا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail also kept his promise to endure sacrifice, as he said in 37:102.
rows.anchor: على الذبح فوفى ، حيث قال : { ستجدنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet begins by directing his own family toward virtue and worship so they model it for others and because they most deserve religious care.
rows.anchor: كان يبدأ بأهله في الأمر بالصلاح والعبادة ليجعلهم قدوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take ahlahu to mean his whole community, relatives and others, since a prophet's people count as his family.
rows.anchor: أمته كلهم من القرابة وغيرهم ؛ لأن أمم النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous person must fully counsel outsiders and especially relatives and close associates, giving them religious benefits without neglect.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن من حق الصالح أن لا يألو نصحا للأجانب فضلا عن الأقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view derives Idrīs from frequent study of scripture and says his original name was Enoch.
rows.anchor: سمي إدريس لكثرة دراسته كتاب الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that derivation: if Idrīs were an afʿīl form from study, proper-name status alone would not make it diptote; its declension pattern indicates foreign origin.
rows.anchor: وهو غير صحيح ؛ لأنه لو كان أفعيلا من الدرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, Iblīs is foreign rather than derived from despair, Yaʿqūb from heel, or Isrāʾīl from Israʾāl as Ibn al-Sikkīt claimed; untrained etymologists make such mistakes.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إبليس أعجمي . وليس من الإبلاس كما يزعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Idrīs may have meant something like 'study' in its original language, leading a narrator to assume the Arabic derivation.
rows.anchor: في تلك اللغة قريبا من ذلك ، فحسبه الراوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His elevated place means the honor of prophethood and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: المكان العلي : شرف النبوة والزلفى عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical reports say Idrīs received thirty scrolls, first wrote with a pen, studied astrology and arithmetic, and first sewed and wore clothes while others wore hides.
rows.anchor: وهو أول من خط بالقلم ونظر في علم النجوم والحساب

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas transmits prophetically that Idrīs was raised to the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه يرفعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Idrīs was raised to the sixth heaven.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إلى السماء السادسة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Idrīs was raised to Paradise, since nothing is higher.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله عنه : إلى الجنة لا شيء أعلى من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī's cited poem says his people's glory reached heaven and they hoped for something higher.
rows.anchor: بلغنا السماء مجدنا وسناؤنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the poem, the Prophet asks where the poet hopes to go and he answers, Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 666 ) ( إلى أين يا أبا ليلى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those points to the prophets named in this surah, from Zachariah through Idrīs.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى المذكورين في السورة من لدن زكريا إلى إدريس عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min in 'among the prophets' is explanatory, as in 48:29, because every prophet received God's favor; the second min is partitive.
rows.anchor: للبيان مثلها في قوله تعالى في آخر سورة الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idrīs descends from Adam and is Noah's paternal grandfather; Abraham descends from Noah's son Shem, and Ishmael from Abraham.
rows.anchor: وكان إدريس من ذرية آدم لقربه منه لأنه جد أبي نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, and John descend from Israel; Jesus does too through Mary.
rows.anchor: وموسى وهارون وزكريا ويحيى من ذرية إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is included among Israel's descendants because Mary descends from him.
rows.anchor: وكذلك عيسى ؛ لأن مريم من ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction in wa-mimman hadaynā may attach to either the first or second min.
rows.anchor: يحتمل العطف على من الأولى والثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If alladhīna is the predicate of ulāʾika, the clause beginning idhā is independent; if it is an adjective, that clause is the predicate.
rows.anchor: إن جعلت الذين خبرا لأولئك كان { إذا تتلى } كلاما مستأنفا

rows.speaker: شبل بن عباد
rows.claim: Shibl ibn ʿAbbād reads yutlā in the masculine because the feminine is nonliteral and a separator intervenes.
rows.anchor: قرأ شبل بن عباد المكي ( يتلى ) بالتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukiyyan is the plural of bākin, like sujūd and quʿūd as plurals of sājid and qāʿid.
rows.anchor: البكي : جمع باك ، كالسجود والقعود

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urges reciting the Qur'an and weeping, or making oneself weep if unable.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 667 )

rows.speaker: صالح المري
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ al-Murrī says that in a dream the Prophet praised his recitation and asked where its weeping was.
rows.anchor: وعن صالح المري رضي الله عنه : قرأت القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas advises delaying prostration at the Israʾ verse until one weeps; if the eyes do not weep, the heart should.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إذا قرأتم سجدة سبحان

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the Qur'an was revealed with grief, so readers should read it sorrowfully.
rows.anchor: إن القرآن أنزل بحزن فإذا قرأتموه فتحازنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People recommend prayers suited to each prostration verse: ask to be among the prostrating at al-Sajda, the humble weepers at al-Isrāʾ, and the guided, prostrating, weeping servants at this verse.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : يدعو في سجدة التلاوة بما يليق بآيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaf with fatḥ commonly denotes successors in good, while khalaf with sukūn denotes successors in evil, like waʿd for a good promise and waʿīd for a threat.
rows.anchor: خلفه : إذا عقبه ، ثم قيل في عقب الخير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the successors as Jews who abandoned obligatory prayer, drank wine, and permitted marriage to a paternal half-sister.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : هم اليهود

rows.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibrahim and Mujahid say they ruined prayer by delaying it.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم ومجاهد رضي الله عنهما : أضاعوها بالتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following exception's reference to repentance and faith supports the first interpretation because it concerns unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وينصر الأول قوله : { إلا من تاب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali glosses following desires with a satirical list: building the imposing, riding the conspicuous, and wearing the famous.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه في قوله : { واتبعوا الشهوات }

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse concerns this Muslim community.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة رضي الله عنه : هو في هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak read al-ṣalawāt in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والحسن والضحاك رضي الله عنهم : ( الصلوات )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, every evil may be called ghayy and every good rashād; al-Muraqqish's verse illustrates that the good are praised and the astray blamed.
rows.anchor: كل شر عند العرب : غي ، وكل خير : رشاد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses ghayyan as recompense for evil, as in 25:68, or as straying from Paradise's path.
rows.anchor: وعن الزجاج : جزاء غي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes Ghayy as a valley in Hell whose valleys seek refuge from it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( غي ) واد في جهنم تستعيذ منه أوديتها

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash reads the verb yalqawna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخفش ( يلقون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both yudkhalūn and yadkhulūn are reported readings.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( يدخلون ) ( ويدخلون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved lose none of their earned reward; rather, it is multiplied, showing that past disbelief does not harm them after repentance.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينقصون شيئا من جزاء أعمالهم ولا يمنعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may mean that no injustice happens at all; alternatively, the idiom mā ẓalamaka an tafʿala means 'what prevented you from doing it'.
rows.anchor: من قولك : ما ظلمك أن تفعل كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens of Eden apposes Paradise because Paradise contains such gardens, like referring to a house and then its chambers and upper rooms.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الجنة مشتملة على جنات عدن أبدلت منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdn may be a definite noun meaning residence, like proper names formed from the concepts of a moment, morning, or yesterday; or it is the name of Paradise's land because it is a dwelling.
rows.anchor: معرفة علم ، بمعنى العدن وهو الإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper-name analyses allow apposition to the definite Paradise and the relative description al-latī; otherwise an indefinite cannot appose a definite unless described.
rows.anchor: لأن النكرة لا تبدل من المعرفة إلا موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings include genitive jannāti ʿadnin and nominative jannātu ʿadnin or jannatu ʿadnin, with the latter as a new subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( جنات عدن ) ( وجنة عدن ) بالرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bil-ghayb may mean Paradise is absent from them, they are absent from it, or they believe in and affirm the unseen.
rows.anchor: وهي غائبة عنهم غير حاضرة . أو هم غائبون عنها لا يشاهدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mātiyyan may be a passive form with active sense; the preferred explanation is that the promise is Paradise, which its inhabitants come to.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن الوعد هو الجنة وهم يأتونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mātiyyan means that the promise was fulfilled, like saying that kindness was rendered to someone.
rows.anchor: أو هو من قولك : أتى إليه إحسانا
